To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tnaph6 was detected in 16 GC1 A. Baumannii isolates, which were recovered from patients in different Iranian hospitals.
the repAci gene was found in 22 A. baumannni isolates from Iran, and 16 of these isolates carried TnaphA on a repA6 plasmid.
the aphA6 resistance gene is carried by the TnaphA-6 transposon on the plasmid repAci6 in A. baumannni isolates from Iran.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of amikacin resistance in A. baumannani isolates in Iran.
the dissemination of Tnrifampin in GC1 A.
the emergence and dissemination of the TnaphA-6 gene in A. baumanniii isolates in Iran.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the repAci plasmid family is involved in the dissemination of aphA6 in A. baumannni isolates.
the repAci family of plasmids is a major contributor to the dissemination of TnaaphA6 among GC1 isolates.
Tnaph6 is disseminating on plasmids encoding the repAci plasmid family in Iranian isolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tnaph6A is not only present in A. baumannani isolates from Iran but it is also found in a variety of repAci plasmids, which may be a potential risk for the dissemination of this resistance gene.
the TnaphA 6-carrying plasmids encoding the repAci 6 gene are widespread among the GC1 A.
Tnapha6 is disseminated in Iran via the GC1 A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aphA6-encoding TnaphA7 plasmid family may be a potential reservoir of resistance genes in A. baumanniii.
Tnapha6 is not restricted to the A. baumanniii strains belonging to GC2, and it can also be present in the strains belonging to other global lineages, such as GC1, in Iran.
Tnapha6-carrying plasmids might be involved in the spread of amikacin resistance among A. baumanniii strains belonging to GC1.
